Joseph Nair
Senior Go Developer | Pimpri-Chinchwad
joseph.nair391@example.com | +91 9420580497

Seasoned backend engineer focused on high-throughput, low-latency services built in Go. Strong track record designing and operating microservices for payments and fantasy-sports platforms, with hands-on experience in containerized deployments and distributed data systems. Open to relocation anywhere in India. Immediate joiner.

Experience

Razorpay, Apr 2025 - Apr 2026
Senior Go Developer — Remote
- Implemented a payments orchestration microservice in Go using gRPC for internal RPC, reducing end-to-end payment routing latency by 28% and improving throughput to 6,000 reqs/sec.
- Containerized services with Docker and deployed to CI pipelines, cutting build-to-deploy time from 45 minutes to 12 minutes and increasing deployment frequency by 3x.
- Designed Postgres schemas and optimized queries, lowering average query time by 40% on critical reconciliation paths and reducing DB CPU usage during peak by 22%.
- Integrated Kafka for event-driven reconciliation, ensuring at-least-once delivery and enabling near-real-time settlement processing with 99.95% success rate.

Saffron Bank, Mar 2025 - Mar 2025
Platform Engineer — Onsite
- Led a one-month PoC to migrate core platform services to Kubernetes, creating Helm charts and operator templates that standardized deployments across staging and production.
- Rewrote critical service bootstrap in Go to support graceful shutdowns and readiness probes, reducing downtime during rolling upgrades to <1 minute per service.
- Automated cluster provisioning and CI/CD pipelines, enabling repeatable deployments and reducing manual intervention by 70%.

Dream11, Nov 2019 - Feb 2025
Go Developer — Hybrid
- Built and scaled microservices in Go for real-time contest management using gRPC between core components, supporting spikes up to 120k concurrent users with <200ms median response times.
- Containerized services and managed Kubernetes deployments, introducing autoscaling and pod disruption budgets that improved availability during high-traffic events to 99.9%.
- Implemented Kafka-based event pipelines for user actions and metrics, increasing observability and enabling faster incident diagnosis; reduced mean time to recovery (MTTR) by 35%.
- Collaborated on Postgres performance tuning and partitioning strategies for large session tables, cutting nightly maintenance windows by 50%.

Projects
- Real-time Match Feed (side project): Go service using gRPC and Kafka to aggregate and publish match events to consumers; Dockerized and tested on a local Kubernetes cluster.
- DB Query Profiler: Tool to capture and analyze Postgres slow queries for Go applications, identifying top regressors and suggesting indexed paths.
